title: Factory functions
summary: A factory makes objects. It keeps object creation in one place so callers do not repeat the setup.
introduction: A factory makes objects. It keeps object creation in one place so callers do not repeat the setup. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A factory makes objects. It keeps object creation in one place so callers do not repeat the setup.

blocks.code:
function makeBook(title) { return { title, borrowed: false }; }
console.log(makeBook("Moon").borrowed);
blocks.title: Factory functions

blocks.text: The call makeBook("Moon") passes Moon into the title parameter. The returned object has title: "Moon" and borrowed: false. Writing .borrowed reads that one property, so the console prints false. Each call returns a fresh book object.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Make two books and change borrowed on only one.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Return a fresh object when callers need independent objects.
For more detail later, use this [Design Patterns further reading](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns).
